newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds up on U.S., rising confidence.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds up on U.S., rising confidence.

text.p: Argentine bonds surged Friday on firm U.S. Treasuries after the U.S. August jobless report and rising confidence that the Argentine government's economic policies will be passed by Congress.

Traders said market activity was busy with prices rising most of the session to close near the day's highs. "Expectations are positive. Bonds are breaking resistance levels," said Hugo Diaz Lourenco, senior analyst at private consultancy C&E Consultores.
The 5.5 percent dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.95 to 116.90. A week ago the bond stood at 115.20.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 rose $1.65 to 97.95.
"The markets have given their vote of confidence," in President Carlos Menem, said Lourenco, refering to Menem's speech Thursday calling for increased unity within the Peronist Party.

Even though nothing concrete has happened since Menem held the speech, it served to raise expectations that the government's recent economic proposals are now more likely to get smooth passage through Congress.
With those rising expectations, Argentine bonds are seen capable of making more gains on the government's economic plans to turn around the budget deficit.

"Brady bonds have grown increasingly fond of fiscal policy and over the medium term, spreads versus comparable Latin instruments should narrow substantially more," said Juan Arranz, Argentina economist at Santander Investments, in an investor note.
